extracted.intended_audience: Attorneys and practitioners who appear before the USPTO (particularly those practicing trademark/non-patent law), USPTO OED staff, and counsel involved in disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: A formal Final Order resolving disciplinary action by the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline concerning an attorney's conduct in trademark (non-patent) matters, including findings, legal conclusions, mitigating factors, and imposed sanctions and procedures for reinstatement/probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction of the USPTO Director / OED
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States Patent and Trademark Office Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26; attorneys authorized to practice trademark and non-patent matters before the Office pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.14(a) are subject to the Disciplinary Rules at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that a licensed attorney (even if not a registered patent practitioner) practicing trademark/non-patent law before the USPTO is within OED jurisdiction and subject to USPTO disciplinary rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Giving false or misleading information to the Office (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4),(b)(5),(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation occurs when a practitioner gives false or misleading information to the Office, as charged under 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(b)(4), (b)(5), and (b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example in this matter: filing electronic petitions to revive that indicated the Office Actions were not received prior to expiration of response periods when facts established otherwise; such representations form the predicate for violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglecting a matter entrusted to the practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner neglects a matter when failing to take necessary steps for representation, such as failing to timely respond to Office actions resulting in abandonment, in violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here, failure to respond to non-final Office actions in a timely manner caused each trademark application to become abandoned as a matter of law; neglect is a basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failing to seek lawful objectives of the client through reasonable available means (37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must seek the lawful objectives of a client through reasonably available means permitted by law; failing to do so violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where respondent's actions (or omissions) prevented lawful pursuit of client objectives, e.g., abandonment due to lack of timely responses and improper representations to revive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to revive and truthfulness of representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to revive abandoned trademark applications (electronic format) that state Office actions were not received prior to expiration are evaluated on the truthfulness of those representations; the Office may grant revives in part based on such representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition to revive contains false or misleading facts about receipt of Office actions, that supports findings of misconduct under the Disciplinary Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factor — absence of prior disciplinary history
rubrics_metrics.description: The absence of any prior disciplinary history before the Office during the respondent's period of licensure is a mitigating factor considered in determining sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case, respondent had no prior disciplinary history during over twelve years licensed, and OED considered that in imposing sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factor — conduct appears aberrational
rubrics_metrics.description: When misconduct appears to be aberrational (out of character), that fact may mitigate the severity of the sanction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order notes the respondent's conduct appears to have been aberrational and treats that as a mitigation point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factor — nexus to medical condition / personal circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence showing a nexus between the misconduct and an existing medical condition or significant personal circumstance (here, a high-risk pregnancy with complications) is a mitigating factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent provided evidence of medical complications concurrent with the filings; OED found sufficient nexus and considered it mitigating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factor — full cooperation with OED
rubrics_metrics.description: Full cooperation with the Office of Enrollment and Discipline during investigation and resolution is a mitigating factor in sanction determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's full cooperation was specifically cited as a reason supporting the agreed sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction — suspension length for trademark/non-patent practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practicing trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO for twenty-four (24) months commencing on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the primary disciplinary sanction imposed for the violations found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to practice for compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date the Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after that date for the sole purpose of facilitating compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary, narrowly-limited practice authorization to allow compliance steps required by 11.58(b). Respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance obligation — 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 as part of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.58 concerns reporting obligations of attorneys disciplined by state bars; compliance is a condition of the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement petition timing and procedure (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may file a petition pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 requesting reinstatement effective prior to expiration of the 24-month suspension any time after two (2) months from the date the Final Order is signed; respondent remains suspended until the OED Director grants reinstatement under § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets minimum time before filing for early reinstatement (two months) and clarifies that actual reinstatement depends on OED Director's grant under the cited regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation following reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: If reinstated, respondent shall serve a twenty-four (24) month period of probation beginning on the date the OED Director reinstates respondent pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation is a required post-reinstatement condition; violations during probation trigger further proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause procedure for probation violations and possible additional suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes respondent failed to comply during probation with any provision of the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause (addressed to the respondent at the Massachusetts Board of Bar Overseers address) and grant 15 days to respond; after consideration, the OED Director may forward materials to the USPTO Director to seek barring reinstatement or additional suspension (up to twenty-two (22) months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two tracks depending on reinstatement status: (A) if not yet reinstated, seek order barring further reinstatement requests until original 24-month suspension is served; (B) if reinstated, seek immediate suspension up to 22 additional months. Any request for review does not stay the Director's order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish this Final Order at the OED Reading Room electronically and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided 'Notice of Suspension' language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must state the respondent's suspension, the Disciplinary Rule violations, eligibility to request reinstatement after two months, probation requirement, and mitigating considerations; disciplinary decisions are posted publicly at the OED Reading Room URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding (including the Final Order) in any further complaint or future disciplinary proceeding against respondent, either as an aggravating factor or to rebut respondent's statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record may be used to increase sanctions in future matters or to counter submissions by respondent; the Order explicitly preserves that ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that no additional cost award between the parties is ordered as part of the settlement.
